parsed_answer.content: A Data Lake is a centralized repository designed to store vast amounts of raw data in its native format, regardless of structure. It operates on the principle of 'schema-on-read,' where data is ingested first and processed later. While effective for massive-scale storage and batch processing, it often devolves into a 'Data Swamp' due to a lack of governance and the bottleneck created by a centralized data engineering team. In contrast, a Data Mesh is a decentralized socio-technical paradigm that treats data as a product. Instead of a monolithic lake, data is owned by cross-functional, domain-oriented teams. These teams are responsible for their own data pipelines, quality, and accessibility via standardized interfaces, typically APIs or event streams. The Data Mesh shifts the focus from 'moving data to a central location' to 'providing data as a service' within the organization.

items: Data Lake internals rely on object storage (S3, GCS) and distributed file systems (HDFS), focusing on high-throughput I/O for analytical engines like Spark or Presto.
Data Mesh relies on 'Federated Computational Governance,' which enforces global standards (security, identity, interoperability) while allowing local autonomy over data modeling.
In a Java-centric ecosystem, Data Mesh often manifests as microservices exposing domain events via Kafka or gRPC, ensuring that the 'data product' is versioned and contract-tested.

Data Lakes often suffer from the 'N+1' problem in data retrieval if not properly partitioned, whereas Data Mesh mitigates this by pushing the responsibility of data optimization to the domain experts who understand the access patterns.

parsed_answer.content: The biggest trap for organizations moving to a Data Mesh is assuming it is purely a technical migration. It is, in reality, an organizational restructuring. If you don't empower domain teams with the budget and autonomy to manage their infrastructure, you will simply end up with a 'Distributed Data Swamp' that is significantly harder to debug than a centralized Data Lake.

title: Explain what a "Data Mesh" is compared to a "Data Lake".
